learning_outcomes.text: Students know and can explain the importance of assembly and handling technology in production.
Students can examine existing assembly systems and formulate suggestions for improvement.
Students can plan rough concepts for assembly and evaluate them.
Students know the basics of assembly planning systematics, workplace design, and handling technology.
Students can abstractly model necessary handling functions.
Students know the particular problems with highly variant assemblies and can identify them, as well as essential approaches to deal with them.
Students can evaluate assembly concepts economically and in terms of their utility.
Students can explain the connection between an MBOM bill of materials structure and the assembly layout, and derive essential approaches for controlling the assembly from it.
Students know essential concepts of digitalization in the specific context of assembly and can evaluate them.
Students can select suitable robots, associated programming methods, and gripping technology for designing value streams in production.
Students are familiar with the structure of industrial robots and their periphery.
Students understand the drivetrain and its control.
Students know mobile robots used in the factory environment for logistics tasks.
Students know path planning methods used to control robots.

syllabus_topics: Importance of assembly and handling technology for production
Organizational forms in assembly
Discussion of different planning cases
Presentation of essential influencing factors for the design of assembly systems
Introduction to exemplary solutions for technical assembly systems
Influences of product design and structure on the design of assembly systems
Procedure for designing assembly systems: process planning, precedence graph and performance balancing
Determination of assembly structure and degree of automation
Creation of the rough layout of an assembly system
Peculiarities of assembly design for highly variant products
Manual, hybrid, and automated assembly systems
Workplace design & ergonomics
Assembly-related provisioning planning
Assembly control
Handling and its sub-functions
Handling devices, transfer systems, and manipulators
Economic aspects of assembly systems
Influences and benefits of digitalization and Industry 4.0 on assembly
Components of a robot system: Kinematics, drivetrain (incl. control), measurement technology, gripping technology, periphery
Different robot types and handling techniques
Methods for programming robots / control technology
Path planning for robots
Mobile robot applications: navigation and path planning for movement tasks
